sections: Boxer engine and ShiftCam
BMW's ShiftCam varies intake valve timing and lift. Its 1,254 cc boxer should not be confused with the preceding R 1200 GS or the subsequent R 1300 GS.
GS and GS Adventure
The standard GS and GS Adventure offer different touring equipment and fuel capacity. Compare the actual trim, luggage and suspension rather than treating both motorcycles as identical.
Adventure touring
The upright riding position, boxer engine and protective bodywork suit extensive road travel and occasional mixed-surface routes.
Sourcing checks
Confirm electronic suspension, rider aids, luggage, service records and whether recalls or software work have been completed.
R 1250 GS launch and development

BMW unveiled the R 1250 GS in September 2018, with European market launches in October. It succeeded the R 1200 GS and introduced a 1,254 cc ShiftCam boxer engine. The 2021 model revision was announced in 2020; the later R 1300 GS belongs to a different model generation. Registration year alone does not establish the specification.
Engine — detailed factory figures

The air/liquid-cooled flat twin uses a 102.5 mm bore and 76 mm stroke, four valves per cylinder, twin overhead camshafts and a 12.5:1 compression ratio. BMW quotes 100 kW (136 PS) at 7,750 rpm and 143 Nm at 6,250 rpm. ShiftCam varies intake valve timing and lift. The drivetrain uses a six-speed gearbox, hydraulically operated wet anti-hopping clutch and shaft final drive.
Dimensions, fuel and wheels

A documented standard R 1250 GS specification lists a 20-litre usable fuel tank, approximately 4-litre reserve, 850/870 mm adjustable seat height, 120/70 R 19 front tyre and 170/60 R 17 rear tyre. A market-specific BMW technical sheet quotes 249 kg road-ready and fully fuelled. Lowered suspension, seats, wheels and market equipment can alter these figures.
Standard GS versus GS Adventure

The R 1250 GS Adventure is a separate model with its own bodywork, larger fuel tank and touring/off-road equipment choices. Do not assume an Adventure specification applies to a standard GS, or that Rallye, Trophy and TE labels indicate identical equipment in every market.
Model-year guide — 2019 to 2023

2019: the new 1,254 cc ShiftCam generation. 2020: early-generation motorcycles continued with equipment and finish dependent on the original order. 2021: EU5 homologation and revised electronics, including Dynamic Traction Control, integral ABS Pro and ECO riding mode in BMW's update. 2022: BMW documented an additional optional aluminium-case holder. 2023: GS Trophy in Gravity Blue Metallic Matte joined the documented style range. Verify the build sheet rather than inferring all features from registration year.
Styles, editions and UK equipment

BMW offered different paint and equipment styles rather than one universal specification: Rallye, Triple Black, GS Trophy and the special 40 Years GS edition are examples. The 40 Years GS edition uses a black-and-yellow theme inspired by the R 100 GS, with gold-coloured details. UK TE is a market equipment designation; check the individual motorcycle for Dynamic ESA, heated grips, cruise control, keyless ride, luggage mounts, shift assistant and riding-mode options.
Factory colours — documented examples

BMW's 2023 model-year information lists Light White (standard), Light White / Racing Blue / Racing Red (Rallye), Black Storm Metallic / Black / Achat Gray (Triple Black) and Gravity Blue Metallic Matte (GS Trophy). BMW's 40 Years GS edition featured black-and-yellow anniversary styling. These are documented examples, not an exhaustive colour-by-year catalogue; check the VIN and original order details for an individual motorcycle.
Electronics and rider assistance

Equipment varies by year, market and options. BMW's 2021 update introduced standard Dynamic Traction Control, integral ABS Pro and ECO riding mode; options included expanded riding modes and adaptive lighting. Dynamic ESA, Gear Shift Assistant Pro, heated seats, cruise control, tyre-pressure monitoring and navigation preparation should be checked against the actual build specification.
Used R 1250 GS inspection checklist

Check service invoices and recalls or outstanding campaigns by VIN; confirm the exact model year and equipment; inspect suspension, Telelever/Paralever joints, wheels, brakes and tyres; examine final-drive condition and leaks; test electronic suspension, TFT display, switchgear, keyless functions and fitted accessories. Confirm pannier frames, luggage keys and any modifications. This is a practical buying checklist, not a claim that all examples develop these faults.
Official BMW technical references

BMW's R 1250 GS technical data provides engine, chassis and dimension figures; BMW Group PressClub records the 2021 revision and model-year updates. Factory press photographs remain linked to BMW's own galleries until AnyBike has explicit permission to republish them.
Chassis, suspension and brakes — factory launch specification

BMW's 2018 R 1250 GS technical sheet specifies Telelever front suspension and a Paralever single-sided rear swingarm, with 190 mm front and 200 mm rear suspension travel. Braking uses twin 305 mm front discs with four-piston radial calipers and a 276 mm rear disc with a two-piston floating caliper. Dynamic ESA was an optional electronically controlled suspension system on the launch specification; confirm the fitted equipment on each motorcycle.
2019 launch equipment versus later updates

The 2019-generation GS had two standard riding modes, Automatic Stability Control (ASC), Hill Start Control, an LED headlight and a 6.5-inch TFT display. Riding Modes Pro could add Dynamic Traction Control, ABS Pro, Hill Start Control Pro and Dynamic Brake Control. Do not describe these early optional features as standard on every 2019 motorcycle. BMW's 2021 revision later made Integral ABS Pro and DTC standard in the published update.
2021 anniversary edition and equipment changes

The 2021 revision included the 40 Years GS anniversary style, with black-and-yellow graphics recalling the R 100 GS. BMW also documented standard ECO mode, USB and 12 V power sockets, with optional adaptive LED headlight, heated rider and passenger seats, 30 mm handlebar risers and expanded riding modes. Availability varied by country and package.
2022 and 2023 factory updates

For the 2022 model year, BMW specifically documented an optional holder for aluminium cases on the R 1250 GS; this should not be presented as a major engine redesign. For 2023, BMW introduced the GS Trophy style in Gravity Blue Metallic with cross-spoke wheels, Rally seat, sport windscreen, radiator and frame protection and Enduro footrests. BMW's global notice said the 40 Years GS edition and Blackstorm metallic finish were no longer available in that model-year range. The US market continued to list a Triple Black style, illustrating why colours and packages must be identified by market.
Wheels, dimensions and carrying capacity — original GS

BMW's 2018 technical sheet lists 3.00 x 19-inch front and 4.50 x 17-inch rear cast wheels, with 120/70 R 19 and 170/60 R 17 tyres. Its original specification records a 2,207 mm overall length, 850/870 mm standard seat positions, 249 kg road-ready weight, 465 kg permitted maximum weight and a 20-litre tank. Accessories, low suspension, spoked wheels and market specifications can change the motorcycle's actual configuration.
Understanding GS styles and factory options

Rallye, Triple Black, GS Trophy and 40 Years GS primarily identify factory style/equipment combinations; they are not separate engine generations. TE is a UK-market equipment description rather than a different engine. A seller's advert may also mix BMW factory packages with dealer-fitted luggage, crash bars, navigation or aftermarket accessories. Use the VIN build specification to confirm what was fitted when new.
BMW factory colour notes by period

At the 2019 launch, BMW described two base finishes and two optional style variants, including HP and Exclusive styling. The 2021 anniversary period added the distinctive black-and-yellow 40 Years GS scheme. For the 2023 US range BMW listed Light White, Rallye in Light White/Racing Blue/Racing Red, Triple Black in Black Storm Metallic/Black/Achat Gray and GS Trophy in Gravity Blue Metallic Matte. These entries describe documented market ranges, not a complete UK year-by-year paint catalogue.
